rationale.summary: Adds 5.5 hours of video production make-up time to replace the Wednesday afternoon editing slot blocked by the mandatory agency photoshoot: 2 hours on Monday evening, 2 hours on Tuesday evening, and 1.5 hours late Wednesday morning. This preserves all fixed/protected events, follows the preference to shift editing toward Monday and Tuesday, and avoids moving audience-facing streams or mandatory health blocks.

weaknesses: The proposal treats the available Monday and Tuesday 18:00-20:00 slots as usable capacity without adequately weighing that they extend already long production days: Gym Workout 10:00-11:30, Video Editing 12:30-18:00, added Video Editing Make-up Block 18:00-20:00, and Live Stream 20:00-23:30 on both 2027-03-22 and 2027-03-23.

Monday and Tuesday create continuous scheduled work from 12:30 to 23:30 with no visible dinner, decompression, stream preparation, or transition margin between editing and live streaming. This is not an objective conflict, but it is a material sustainability risk for focus and on-camera performance.

The Wednesday added block from 11:30-13:00 starts immediately after the fixed Gym Workout 10:00-11:30 and leaves only 13:00-14:00 before the fixed Talent Agency Photoshoot & Meeting. The rationale accounts for not filling the full interval until 14:00, but it does not discuss whether immediate post-gym editing is practically usable given hygiene, food, preparation, and any downtown travel/setup needs.

The alternatives considered are mostly about protecting fixed events and avoiding external dependencies. They do not sufficiently consider human-capacity alternatives such as reducing the amount recovered within this visible horizon, using smaller blocks, preserving a break before streams, or otherwise substantiating why the compressed Monday/Tuesday evenings are sustainable.

The final calendar’s added events have null category, importance, participants, and description despite the proposal describing them as video_production blocks with importance 4 and user participation. The metadata note says this is contractual rather than a new preference issue, so it is not treated as a technical violation, but it makes the resulting calendar less self-explanatory.
critic_evaluation.feedback: The proposal is technically tidy and gives a clear rationale for protecting sleep, gym, the agency event, and audience-facing streams. However, the human workload created by the additions is only partly justified. The most important concern is the Monday and Tuesday pattern: after a protected gym workout, the user has 5.5 hours of existing editing, then 2 added hours of make-up editing, then a 3.5-hour live stream, with the added blocks directly touching both the existing editing and the streams. Across two consecutive days, that is a demanding production-to-performance sequence with no visible evening recovery or meal margin. Wednesday is also tight because the new editing block begins immediately after gym and precedes a fixed agency photoshoot and meeting by one hour. This may still be workable for this user, especially if they routinely eat during work, need minimal stream setup, and can recover adequately after late streams, but the rationale does not substantiate those conditions. The proposer should reconsider whether full recovery of the blocked editing time within these exact compressed slots is necessary, or provide a grounded explanation from its fuller context that the user can sustainably handle these back-to-back work, exercise, and streaming demands. Request satisfaction cannot be independently verified because the original request is not available; this review only assesses the visible proposal, rationale, validation, and resulting calendar.

rationale.summary: Adds 5.5 hours of video production make-up time without moving any fixed, protected, or audience-facing events. Compared with the earlier plan, the recovery is distributed across the week: 1 hour Monday evening, 1 hour Tuesday evening, 30 minutes Wednesday midday, and 1.5 hours each on Thursday and Friday split between midday and evening. This still gives Monday and Tuesday priority, but preserves visible pre-stream buffers and avoids placing a long editing block immediately after Wednesday gym or immediately before the fixed downtown agency event. The trade-off is fragmentation: several shorter blocks may be less efficient for deep editing than one long session, and the calendar still cannot verify meals, travel, showering, or recovery needs because those details were not supplied.

weaknesses: The revision materially improves the prior Monday/Tuesday problem by shortening the added evening blocks to 18:00-19:00 and leaving 19:00-20:00 before the 20:00-23:30 live streams. However, Monday and Tuesday still become demanding days: Gym Workout 10:00-11:30, existing Video Editing 12:30-18:00, added make-up editing 18:00-19:00, then Live Stream 20:00-23:30.

The new distribution shifts some load to Thursday and Friday, where the added 12:00-12:30 blocks begin only 30 minutes after Gym Workout 10:00-11:30 and then connect directly into existing Video Editing 12:30-18:00 plus added make-up editing 18:00-19:00. That creates a long 12:00-19:00 production stretch on both 2027-03-25 and 2027-03-26, followed by only one visible hour before each live stream.

Across the visible week, the proposed additions mean every weekday contains a fixed gym workout, a substantial production or agency commitment, and a 20:00-23:30 live stream. Much of that workload pre-exists, but the added 5.5 hours reduce recovery and personal-time space across the whole horizon rather than leaving any visibly lighter weekday.

The proposal acknowledges fragmentation, but several 30-minute make-up blocks, especially 2027-03-24 12:15-12:45, 2027-03-25 12:00-12:30, and 2027-03-26 12:00-12:30, may be less effective for video editing if setup, task-switching, rendering, or context-loading time is significant. This is not an objective conflict, but it affects whether the recovered time is practically equivalent to the displaced 5.5-hour editing slot.

The resulting calendar still has null category, importance, participants, and description on added events, despite the proposal describing them as video_production blocks with importance 4 and user participation. The metadata note explains this as a contract issue rather than a human preference or technical failure, but it makes the final calendar less self-explanatory.
critic_evaluation.feedback: The revised proposal gives a grounded answer to the prior review’s main concern. It no longer places two-hour make-up editing blocks directly against Monday and Tuesday streams, and it reduces the Wednesday post-gym/pre-agency pressure by using only 12:15-12:45 with visible space before and after. The rationale also explicitly weighs meals, decompression, setup, recovery, concentration of workload, and audience-facing dependencies, which is stronger than simply using free slots. The remaining concern is cumulative rather than a clear contradiction: the plan adds production capacity on every weekday of an already heavy visible routine. Thursday and Friday in particular now run from gym into a short midday make-up block, existing editing, another make-up block, then a live stream after a one-hour gap. That may be sustainable for this user, and the proposal’s distribution is plausible given the visible goal of recovering 5.5 hours without moving fixed or audience-facing events. Still, the plan depends on the user being able to use short editing blocks effectively and handle compressed post-gym and pre-stream routines. Request satisfaction cannot be independently verified because the original request is unavailable; this review only assesses the visible proposal, rationale, validation, prior review, and resulting calendar.

plausibility_review.suggested_improvement: If the Proposer has fuller context, it should briefly substantiate that the user can make productive use of the short 30-minute editing blocks and can handle the Thursday/Friday 12:00-19:00 production stretches with only the visible pre-stream buffer. If that context is not available, retain the assumptions rather than treating the free slots as proof of comfort.

weaknesses: The proposal treats the available Monday and Tuesday 18:00-20:00 slots as usable capacity without adequately weighing that they extend already long production days: Gym Workout 10:00-11:30, Video Editing 12:30-18:00, added Video Editing Make-up Block 18:00-20:00, and Live Stream 20:00-23:30 on both 2027-03-22 and 2027-03-23.

Monday and Tuesday create continuous scheduled work from 12:30 to 23:30 with no visible dinner, decompression, stream preparation, or transition margin between editing and live streaming. This is not an objective conflict, but it is a material sustainability risk for focus and on-camera performance.

The Wednesday added block from 11:30-13:00 starts immediately after the fixed Gym Workout 10:00-11:30 and leaves only 13:00-14:00 before the fixed Talent Agency Photoshoot & Meeting. The rationale accounts for not filling the full interval until 14:00, but it does not discuss whether immediate post-gym editing is practically usable given hygiene, food, preparation, and any downtown travel/setup needs.

The alternatives considered are mostly about protecting fixed events and avoiding external dependencies. They do not sufficiently consider human-capacity alternatives such as reducing the amount recovered within this visible horizon, using smaller blocks, preserving a break before streams, or otherwise substantiating why the compressed Monday/Tuesday evenings are sustainable.

The final calendar’s added events have null category, importance, participants, and description despite the proposal describing them as video_production blocks with importance 4 and user participation. The metadata note says this is contractual rather than a new preference issue, so it is not treated as a technical violation, but it makes the resulting calendar less self-explanatory.
prior_critic_reviews.feedback: The proposal is technically tidy and gives a clear rationale for protecting sleep, gym, the agency event, and audience-facing streams. However, the human workload created by the additions is only partly justified. The most important concern is the Monday and Tuesday pattern: after a protected gym workout, the user has 5.5 hours of existing editing, then 2 added hours of make-up editing, then a 3.5-hour live stream, with the added blocks directly touching both the existing editing and the streams. Across two consecutive days, that is a demanding production-to-performance sequence with no visible evening recovery or meal margin. Wednesday is also tight because the new editing block begins immediately after gym and precedes a fixed agency photoshoot and meeting by one hour. This may still be workable for this user, especially if they routinely eat during work, need minimal stream setup, and can recover adequately after late streams, but the rationale does not substantiate those conditions. The proposer should reconsider whether full recovery of the blocked editing time within these exact compressed slots is necessary, or provide a grounded explanation from its fuller context that the user can sustainably handle these back-to-back work, exercise, and streaming demands. Request satisfaction cannot be independently verified because the original request is not available; this review only assesses the visible proposal, rationale, validation, and resulting calendar.

rationale.summary: Adds 5.5 hours of video production make-up time without moving any fixed, protected, or audience-facing events. Compared with the earlier plan, the recovery is distributed across the week: 1 hour Monday evening, 1 hour Tuesday evening, 30 minutes Wednesday midday, and 1.5 hours each on Thursday and Friday split between midday and evening. This still gives Monday and Tuesday priority, but preserves visible pre-stream buffers and avoids placing a long editing block immediately after Wednesday gym or immediately before the fixed downtown agency event. The trade-off is fragmentation: several shorter blocks may be less efficient for deep editing than one long session, and the calendar still cannot verify meals, travel, showering, or recovery needs because those details were not supplied.
